PS 8.2 | Electric Field and Charge

Problems

  1. A point charge of +3.0 μC is placed at the origin. What is the magnitude and direction of the electric field 25 cm away from the charge along the x-axis?
  1. Two charges, +2.0 μC and -2.0 μC, are placed 40 cm apart on the x-axis. Calculate the net electric field at a point exactly midway between them.
  1. Three point charges are arranged at the corners of an equilateral triangle (side 0.50 m): +4.0 μC at A, +4.0 μC at B, and -4.0 μC at C. Find the magnitude and direction of the net electric field at the center of the triangle.
  1. A charge of -6.0 μC is located 30 cm from a point P. What is the electric potential at point P due to this charge? How much work is required to bring a +1.0 μC charge from infinity to point P?
  1. A parallel plate capacitor has a capacitance of 8.0 μF and is charged to a potential difference of 15 V. Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor.
  1. The plates of a parallel plate capacitor are moved farther apart while keeping the charge constant. Explain qualitatively what happens to the electric field, potential difference, and stored energy.
  1. Sketch the electric field lines and equipotential surfaces for a system of two equal but opposite charges separated by a small distance (an electric dipole). Describe the pattern and explain the relationship between field lines and equipotentials.
  1. A small test charge is placed near a large, positively charged conducting sphere. Describe and explain the direction of the electric field and the force experienced by the test charge both outside and inside the sphere.

Answers

  1. 4.3 × 10^5 N/C, directed away from the charge along the x-axis

  2. 0 N/C (fields cancel at the midpoint)

  3. 8.0 × 10^5 N/C, directed from the center toward the negative charge

  4. -1.8 × 10^5 V; -0.18 J

  5. 9.0 × 10^-4 J

  6. Electric field remains constant, potential difference increases, stored energy increases.

  7. Field lines emerge from the positive charge and enter the negative charge; equipotentials are perpendicular to field lines and crowd near the charges.

  8. Outside: field points radially outward, force repels positive test charge; inside: field is zero, no force on the test charge.
